en: The Sūtra on the Ritual Manual for the Visualization of the Great Mantras of the Ten Wrathful Vidyārājas from the Mahāyoga Teaching of the *Māyājāla* (The Net of Illusion),
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao San Dafu, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

Translated by the Imperial Subject Dharma-bhadra, the Great Master Mingjiao, by Imperial Decree. At that time, the World-Honored One was in the Pure Great Pavilion within the Heaven of Purity and Radiance (*Śuddhāvāsa*). That pavilion was adorned with various vajra pillars and the most supreme precious jewels; such magnificent decorations and offerings were entirely the miraculous transformations of the Tathāgata’s supernatural powers.
At that time, there were Tathāgatas such as Akṣobhya, Ratnasaṃbhava, Amitāyus, and Amoghasiddhi within the assembly.
Then, from the four gates of the womb-matrix (garbha) of the Great Vairocana Tathāgata, there emerged an infinite multitude of great Bodhisattvas, vidyās, and worthy sages.
Furthermore, there were wrathful vidyārājas together with their retinues— Citta and Citī, Natta and Nate, Kinkara and Kinkarī—
as well as countless hosts of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and others, all of whom came together to the assembly and surrounded the Bhagavān.

At that time, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana dwelt perpetually in the samādhi of peaceful bliss, never departing from great wisdom, great practice, and great kindness and compassion to rescue and deliver sentient beings.
At that time, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, having gazed upon the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi within the great assembly, emitted a great radiance that illuminated the gathered multitude.

Then the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, gazed up at the Tathāgata, and casting his vajra with his right hand, knelt with his right knee upon the ground, joined his palms in salutation, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"By what cause and by what condition has the Tathāgata emitted this great radiance?"
If there were no cause or condition, the Buddha would not emit this light.
Seeing this light, doubt has arisen in my mind; the great assembly gathered here is likewise filled with uncertainty.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will let out a lion’s roar and skillfully expound the wondrous Dharma to sever the web of my doubts.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, having accepted the request of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, spoke these words:
"I shall now emit light rays, desiring to proclaim this Great King of Tantras of Yoga, the Great Wisdom, Great Sovereign Net of Illusory Transformations."

Vajrapāṇi! This practice of the skillful means of the great wisdom-vajra is the most supreme among all that is performed within the ocean of all meanings; it is the highest among the high within all teachings, and is able to bring perfect peace and happiness to all sentient beings.
Having spoken thus, he immediately entered the *samādhi* of the Great Bliss Vajra, the Great Sovereign Vajra of Wisdom and Skillful Means for Deliverance.
Emerging from that concentration, he taught the ritual procedure for the visualization of the ten wrathful vidyārājas within the samaya maṇḍala of the Great Yoga of the Net of Great Māyā.
Furthermore, the vidyādhara practitioner should form the visualization of the great wisdom through the syllable HŪṂ.
This syllable HŪṂ transforms into the wrathful Great Vidyārāja Yamāntaka, with light like the fire at the end of an eon.
His body is the color of a great dark-blue cloud; he has six faces, six arms, and six feet, with a short stature and a large belly, appearing in a state of great wrath.
His wrathful aspect features sharp fangs like vajras and three eyes on each face;
he is adorned by the eight great nāga kings, wears a tiger-skin garment and a crown of skulls, and rides upon a water buffalo while treading upon lotus flowers.
His beard is reddish-yellow, he possesses great eloquence, and he bears the Buddha Akṣobhya as his crest-jewel.

Seated there, they looked at one another with great malice; the front face smiled, the right face was yellow with its tongue protruding, and the left face was white with its lips bitten—this was the emanation of the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī.
The first right hand holds a sword, the second holds a vajra, and the third holds an arrow.
The first left hand holds a noose with the index finger extended upward, the second holds the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, and the third holds a bow.
Beneath this Vidyārāja, one should visualize all the celestial Māras prostrating in fear; his body possesses a solar disc with a circular halo, and emanations of various Buddhas appear like clouds.

If the vidyādhara thus contemplates according to the ritual and recites the Great Mantra, that person—whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining—will constantly enjoy the pleasures of the five senses without transgression, just as space cannot be defiled by material objects. This is called the Great Wisdom Vajra Subduing Samādhi capable of both creation and destruction.
Furthermore, the Bhagavān, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, who is the foremost of all Tathāgatas, entered the vajra-samādhi of the Great Wisdom Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he spoke this Great Mantra of the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Yamāntaka through the three vajra-gates:
*Namo siddhi-vajrāṇām | Oṃ kha kha* (Note: *Vajrāṇām* is drawn out with a long vowel;
*kha* is pronounced as a sharp, aspirated sound.)

*Sadaya svāhā.* (57) At that time, when the Great Vairocana Tathāgata had spoken this great vidyā-mantra, all the Buddhas and the Bodhisattvas of great majesty and virtue marveled at what they had never before experienced, and they focused their minds solely upon the Great Vajra Vairocana Buddha.

"Just as this Great Wisdom, Great Transformation, Vajra Great Wrathful Yamāntaka of Great Power has appeared in the world, so too does the vidyādhara who binds the boundary according to the ritual law become supreme in eliminating all evils."

"Furthermore, when the Vidyādhara performs the rite of accomplishment, he should use the skull of one who has died naturally; it must be a single, complete, and well-formed piece with both ear-sockets intact, fit for the performance of the ritual."
If the skull is composed of two halves and the two ear-cavities do not penetrate through, it is unfit for ritual practice.

Take earth from beneath the feet of a Śūdra to form a paste, fashion the image of a Śūdra, and place it inside the skull. The mantra-holder should tread upon it with his foot and recite this Great Mantra to summon him quickly; by visualizing in this manner, he shall be subdued.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Great Vairocana Vajra Tathāgata, further taught the visualization method for the Unconquerable Great Wrathful Vidyārāja:

"The syllable *praḥ* is the Great Wisdom. Visualize the syllable *praḥ* transforming into the Unconquerable Great Wrathful Vidyārāja, with three faces, each with three eyes and six arms; his body is yellow, with a solar halo of radiant light, dwelling in sovereign splendor and vast illumination. He is adorned by the eight great Nāga kings. His front face has a smiling expression; his right face is a deep blue with a slight wrathful aspect; his left face is white, biting his lip and manifesting a great fierce appearance."
The first right hand holds a vajra; the second holds a jeweled staff; the third holds an arrow.
The first left hand holds a noose with the index finger extended upward; the second holds the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra; the third holds a bow.
Visualizing in this manner, one manifests the signs of formation and destruction, and bears the Buddha Akṣobhya upon the crown of the head.
If one recites according to the ritual, one will swiftly attain perfect awakening; this is called the "Invincible Great Wisdom Vajra Samādhi."
At that time, after the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, had spoken this visualization, he entered the samādhi of the Great Amoghasiddhi-Vajramukha-Amitābha-Raudra-Vajra.
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he spoke this great vidyā-mantra of the invincible Great Wrathful Vidyārāja through the three vajra-gates:
"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | Namaḥ vajrakrodhāya ||"

At that time, when the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, had spoken this great vidyā-mantra of the invincible Great Wrathful Vidyārāja, all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of great majesty and virtue offered praise; all the māras, heterodox teachers, and others were struck with great terror, their bodies trembling and their minds shaken, thinking only of the Buddha Mahāvairocana.

Furthermore, when a Vidyādhara performs the rite of accomplishment, he should take leaves from within a whirlwind and earth from beneath the feet of a Śatru, mix them together, and fashion the form of a Piśāca. The Vidyādhara should step upon it with his foot and recite this Great Mantra according to the ritual rules. By employing the syllable *HŪṂ* (𑖬) along with the syllable *VAṂ* (𑖮) together with the Vidyā, he can even dispatch Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, let alone a Śatru.
Furthermore, regarding the method of visualization: visualize the syllable *HŪṂ* as Great Wisdom.

It transforms into the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Pañjaranātha, with three faces, each having three eyes and eight arms. The central face has a smiling expression; the right face is a deep blue color with its tongue protruding like a vajra; the left face is yellow with sharp fangs baring its lips. He is clothed in a tiger skin. His first right hand holds a vajra, the second a jeweled staff, the third a *kanaya*, and the fourth an arrow.

The first left hand holds a noose with the index finger extended; the second hand holds the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra; the third hand holds a lotus; and the fourth hand holds a bow. One should visualize these as having the appearance of formation and destruction, capable of manifesting countless Buddhas, and crowned by Akṣobhya Buddha. If one visualizes according to the ritual method, one will surely attain accomplishment; this is called the Supreme Hayagrīva Vajra Samādhi.

At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava Mahāvajra entered the *samādhi* of the Great Wisdom Vajra of Jewel Transformation. Emerging from that concentration, he spoke this great vidyā-mantra of the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Pañjaranātha:

*Namo samantabuddhānām | Oṃ jina-līḍi | ṭa hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.* When the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, had spoken this great vidyā-mantra of the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Pañjaranātha, all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas offered their praise. The rākṣasas, bhūtas, nāginīs, skandhas, and all the grahas were utterly terrified, trembling with fear.
That vidyādhara, reciting according to the ritual, manifests all signs of accomplishment and destruction.
Furthermore, the visualization method for this great wrathful vidyārāja Vajrajanmadeha is explained as follows: "The syllable HŪṂ is Great Wisdom;

visualize it transforming into the great wrathful vidyārāja Vajrajanmadeha, the color of a great blue cloud, with three faces and six arms. Each face has three eyes; the central face is smiling, the right face is white, and the left face is yellow, displaying a wrathful expression with bared fangs. His right foot treads upon various māras, and his left foot treads upon a lotus flower."
The first right hand holds a sharp sword; the second hand holds a battle-axe; the third hand holds an arrow.
The first left hand holds a lasso with the index finger extended; the second hand holds the *Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*; the third hand holds a bow.
Bearing Akṣobhya Buddha upon one’s crown, endowed with great supernormal powers, one is able to subdue all demonic transformations and rain down great compassion.
Thus, by contemplating according to the ritual method, one eliminates all demons; this is called the Supreme Great Vajra Samādhi.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Great Vajra Tathāgata of Immeasurable Life, entered the Great Vajra Samādhi of the Precious Treasury of Immeasurable Merit.
Emerging from this meditative absorption, he spoke this great vidyā-mantra of the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Vighnāntaka: "Namo samantabuddhānām."

[62] At that time, when the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Amitāyus, had spoken this great vidyā-mantra of the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Vajrakuṇḍalī, the entire great assembly was struck with terror and thought only of the Buddha Vairocana, who possesses great wisdom, is a great vajra, and is endowed with great compassion.

"If a vidyādhara visualizes a lotus within his palm, and within that lotus visualizes the syllable HŪṂ, which is filled with great blazing flames—by means of such a samādhi of the Wrathful Vidyārāja, he can eliminate all poisons throughout the three realms."
Furthermore, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, taught this visualization method for the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Acala:

"The syllable *Haṃ* is the Great Wisdom; visualize it transforming into the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Acala, with the appearance of a squint-eyed youth (*kumāra*), six arms and three faces, each with three eyes, adorned with the ornaments of a youth."

The front face has a smiling expression; from the right face, a yellow tongue protrudes, its tip tinged with the color of blood; the left face is white and wrathful, emitting the sound of the syllable HŪṂ.

The body is the color of emerald; the feet tread upon lotus flowers and jeweled mountains; standing in a dancing posture, he is able to eliminate all māras; his entire body is ablaze with flames and a circular halo like the sun’s orb.
The first right hand holds a sword, the second holds a vajra, and the third holds an arrow.
The first left hand holds a noose with the index finger extended, the second holds the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, and the third holds a bow.
Wearing a Buddha-crown, he is an emanation of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya.
Possessing great supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), he manifests various Buddhas like clouds.

When that vidyādhara visualizes in this manner, unsurpassed bodhi will be accomplished before long; this is called the "Samādhi of the Great Wisdom and Great Sovereignty of the Vajra of All Tathāgatas’ Immovable [Nature]."
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, entered the Vajra-samādhi of the Blazing Great Radiance of the Vajra Lamp.
Emerging from this meditative absorption, he spoke this great mantra of the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Acala: "Namo samantabuddhānām."

*Asaha namaḥ svāhā.* (44) At that time, when the World-Honored One, the Great Vairocana Tathāgata, had spoken this great vidyā-mantra of the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Acala, all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, kiṃnaras, and various māras were struck with great terror. As if scorched by a great fire, they fell to the ground in confusion and distress, thinking only of the Buddha Mahāvairocana.

"In this way, the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Acala is able to summon the celestial maidens and cause them all to be terrified, swiftly accomplishing various desired tasks; he is the manifestation of the supernatural powers of the Tathāgata Vairocana."
Furthermore, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana expounded this visualization method for the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Ṭakkirāja:

"The syllable *HŪṂ* [with the vowel *Ā*] constitutes great wisdom; visualize it transforming into the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Ṭakkirāja, with three faces, each with three eyes, and six arms, wearing a jeweled crown upon his head, in which a Buddha resides."

The Vidyārāja has hanging hair and a smiling expression on his front face; his right face is yellow with a frowning brow; his left face is white and wrathful, biting its lip; his body is the color of blue clouds, surrounded by a circular halo of solar radiance.
The two hands on both sides form the fundamental mudrā; the second right hand holds a vajra, and the third right hand holds an arrow;
the second left hand holds the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, and the third left hand holds a bow.
Standing with feet treading upon lotuses in a dancing posture, he transforms all Buddhas, while the various Māras below are struck with terror.
That vidyādhara who visualizes according to the rite will swiftly realize Bodhi; this mantra is called the "Invoking All Supreme Vajra Samādhi."
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, entered the *vajra-samādhi* known as the "Pervasive Blazing Treasury.
Emerging from this meditative absorption, he spoke this great vidyā-mantra of the Great Wrathful King Takkirāja:

*Namo samantabuddhānām | Oṃ takki hūṃ jaḥ.* When the World-Honored One, the Great Vairocana Tathāgata, had spoken this great vidyā-mantra of the Great Wrathful King Takkirāja, all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas offered their praise, while all the māras became utterly bewildered and fainted, falling prostrate to the ground.
Furthermore, the method for accomplishment is explained:

"At that time, the vidyādhara, performing the rite according to the method of the Buddha Amoghasiddhi, should step upon the form of Śatru with his right foot, manifesting a great wrathful appearance with knitted brows; he is able to summon all māras and destroy all mantra-rites, causing all sentient beings to give rise to a heart of reverence and love."
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Great Vajra Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, spoke this visualization method for the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Nīlananda:
"The syllable HŪṂ is the Great Wisdom; visualize it transforming into the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Nīlananda, with three faces, each with three eyes, and six arms."

The front face is blue and displays a smile; the left face is yellow, and the right face is white with its lips bitten. The body is the color of blue clouds, adorned with the eight great nāga kings. His hair-knot is lush and dark blue, and he bears the Buddha upon his crown. He stands upon a lotus flower in a dancing posture.
The first right hand holds a vajra; the second holds a jeweled staff; the third holds an arrow.

The first left hand holds a lasso with the index finger extended upward; the second holds the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra; the third holds a bow with a solar disc halo, manifesting all Buddhas like clouds. This is called the Great Wisdom Vajra Samādhi for Subduing and Eliminating Māra’s Enemies.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Great Vajra Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, entered the great vajra-samādhi of the supreme jewel-bannered great maṇi, the Source of the Unfailing.
Having emerged from samādhi, he spoke this great dhāraṇī-mantra of the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Mahānīlananda:
"Namaḥ samantabuddhānām | Oṃ īkṣe he vagvan."

the Great Vajra Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, had thus spoken this great mantra of the Vidyārāja Nīladanda, all the palaces of the Māras in the lands of the ten directions trembled violently, and they could think of nothing but the Great Vairocana Buddha of the Three Vajras.

“That Vidyādhara shall achieve accomplishment in all mudrās and through the ritual application of this great mantra; if one recites this great mantra eight hundred times, one can slay all māras and adversaries.”
Furthermore, the visualization method for the Great Powerful Wrathful Vidyārāja is taught as follows: "The syllable *HŪṂ* is the Great Wisdom;

visualize it transforming into the Great Powerful Great Wrathful Vidyārāja, with three faces, each with three eyes, and eight arms. His body is the color of blue clouds, adorned by the eight great nāga kings. Blazing flames pervade his entire body, and his hair stands upright. His eyes are a deep crimson, and he bears Akṣobhya Buddha upon his crown."

The central face is smiling; the right face is golden, and the left face is white with bared fangs. He tramples upon lotuses, manifesting a great wrathful form that strikes terror into the gods, who flee in all directions. He is encircled by a halo of solar radiance.
The first right hand holds a vajra; the second holds a jeweled staff; the third holds a sword; and the fourth holds an arrow.
The first left hand holds a noose with the index finger extended; the second holds the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra; the third holds a *gandī* (wooden gong); and the fourth holds a bow.
"The emanations of all Buddhas are like clouds;
this visualization is called the Samādhi of the Great Power, Great Wisdom, and Supreme Great Vajra.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya Mahāvajra, entered the Samādhi of the Universal Emanation and Adornment of the Great Vajra.
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he spoke this great mantra of the Great Powerful Wrathful Vidyārāja:
"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | oṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ."

PHAṬ PHAṬ PHAṬ | NAVA MAHĀMĀRAYĀYA SVĀHĀ || (10) At that time,

when the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, had spoken this great vidyā-mantra of the Great Powerful Wrathful King, all the celestial Māras were utterly terrified and thought only of the Vajra Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
"The Vidyādhara who recites this great mantra can grant all wishes; even for stopping rain or seeking rain, there is nothing that does not accord with his will.
Furthermore, the Great Tathāgata Mahāvairocana-Vajra spoke this visualization method for the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Sumbha:

"The syllable HŪṂ is Great Wisdom. Visualize it transforming into the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Sumbha, whose body is a deep blue color. With his first left and right hands, he forms the fundamental mudrā; his second right hand holds a sword, and his third right hand holds an arrow."
The second left hand holds the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, and the third hand holds a bow.
This Great Vidyārāja possesses the most supreme power within the three realms.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, spoke this great vidyā-mantra of the Great Wrathful King Pañjaranātha:

*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | Oṃ saṃbhani saṃbha hūṃ | Kṛṇa kṛṇa hūṃ | Kṛṇa paca | Kṛṇa paca hūṃ | Ānaya ho bhagavan | Vinyarāja hūṃ phaṭ.* At that time, when the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, had spoken this great vidyā-mantra of the Great Wrathful King Saṃbhara, all the goddesses were struck with terror; they clasped the feet of the vidyā-king and thought only of the Greatly Wise Buddha Mahāvairocana.

"This great vidyā possesses immense power; it acts as a vajra-noose and a vajra-hook, compelling all goddesses and others to come swiftly without exception. Among all methods of invocation, this vidyā is the most supreme."
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, further taught the visualization method for the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Vajrapātāla:
"The syllable *Ḍa* represents great wisdom; visualize it transforming into the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Vajrapātāla, whose body is the color of white milk and who has six arms."
The first right hand holds a vajra, the second holds a vajrāṅkuśa, and the third holds an arrow.
The first left hand holds a pāśa with the index finger extended, the second holds the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, and the third holds a bow; he manifests the form of one who subdues all asuras.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, spoke this great vidyā-mantra of the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Vajrapātāla:
"Oṃ vraja sarvapātālanaivedyagaṇa hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ. Then the World-Honored One, the Vajra Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, said:
"These ten great wrathful vidyārājas each have three faces, with three eyes on each face; the eyes are a deep crimson color, and they manifest the appearance of wrathful glances."

He is adorned with the eight great nāga kings: the black nāga king Nanda and the nāga king Kūlika are bound in his topknot; the golden nāga king Takṣaka serves as his earrings; the reddish-gold nāga king Mahāpadma serves as his bracelets; the white nāga king Karkoṭaka serves as his shoulder-cloth; the red-lotus-colored nāga king Vāsuki serves as his waist-belt; and the white, conch-like nāga king Padma serves as the bells upon his feet. Thus, these eight great nāga kings constitute his ornaments.

These ten great Vidyārājas all manifest fierce and terrible forms; they wear tiger skins as garments and skulls as crowns, their topknots stand upright and are reddish-yellow in color, and each bears Akṣobhya Tathāgata upon their heads. Each possesses a solar disc halo and a seat; their front faces display smiling expressions, their right faces slightly manifest wrathful features, and their left faces exhibit great ferocity. With sharp fangs biting their lips and furrowed brows, they stand in a dancing posture. For those who hold the vidyā-mantras, if they visualize them according to the ritual, there shall be no wish that is not fulfilled.
The Sūtra of the Ritual Manual for the Visualization of the Great Mantras of the Ten Wrathful Vidyārājas from the Mahāyoga Teaching of the Māyājāla Net, Spoken by the Buddha.
